question: Which of these MFIs are NOT regulated by the RBI?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Non-profit MFIs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) in India operate under four broad models, and the RBI directly regulates only the for-profit, company-form lenders among them. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थाएं — गैर-लाभकारी एमएफआई RBI के दायरे से बाहर)

 

• Non-profit MFIs are entities registered as Societies (under the Societies Registration Act), Trusts (under the Indian Trusts Act), or Section 8 (not-for-profit) Companies. Since they do not accept public deposits and are not structured as NBFCs, they fall outside the RBI's direct regulatory perimeter and are instead governed by their respective registering statutes/state money-lending laws.

 

• In contrast, NBFC-MFIs, Bank-led MFIs, and Small Finance Bank-led MFIs are all regulated by the RBI, primarily through the RBI's Master Directions on NBFC-MFIs and general banking regulation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI's regulatory framework for NBFC-MFIs covers aspects such as capital adequacy, loan pricing (interest rate caps), and household income-based lending limits, introduced to protect borrowers from over-indebtedness.

 

• Sa-Dhan and MFIN are the two RBI-recognised Self-Regulatory Organisations (SROs) for the microfinance sector.

 

NOTE

 

• Small Finance Bank led MFIs (Option 1): Small Finance Banks are licensed and regulated by the RBI under the Banking Regulation Act.

 

• Bank led MFIs (Option 2): Commercial banks undertaking microfinance lending are regulated by the RBI as banks.

 

• NBFC MFIs (Option 3): These are directly regulated by the RBI under the NBFC-MFI Master Directions.

question: Pandit Birju Maharaj is associated with which form of dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj (1938-2022) was a legendary exponent of Kathak, belonging to the Kalka-Bindadin Gharana (Lucknow Gharana). (कथक नृत्य — पंडित बिरजू महाराज)

 

• He was a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan (1986) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, and served as a guru at Kalashram, the institution he founded for Kathak training.

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, traditionally associated with storytelling through rhythmic footwork, spins (chakkars), and expressive gestures (abhinaya), originating in North India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight classical dances of India are: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

• Birju Maharaj also composed music and choreographed dance sequences for several Bollywood films, including *Devdas* and *Bajirao Mastani*.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhau (Option 2): A tribal martial-dance form from Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal, not one of Birju Maharaj's forms.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 3): A classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Kathakali (Option 4): A classical dance-drama form from Kerala, distinct from Kathak despite the similar-sounding name.

question: Which cell organelles are known as cell's post office?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golgi apparatus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Golgi apparatus (Golgi body/Golgi complex) is called the "post office of the cell" because it packages, modifies, sorts and dispatches proteins and lipids to their correct destinations, inside or outside the cell. (गॉल्जी उपकरण — कोशिका का डाकघर)

 

• It was discovered by the Italian scientist Camillo Golgi in 1898, and consists of a stack of flattened, membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.

 

• It plays a key role in the modification (e.g., glycosylation), packaging and secretion of materials synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum, and also forms lysosomes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mitochondrion is called the "powerhouse of the cell" as it generates ATP.

 

• The Endoplasmic Reticulum is called the cell's "transport system/manufacturing unit", and Lysosomes are called the "suicide bags" of the cell.

 

NOTE

 

• Nucleus (Option 1): Called the "control centre/brain" of the cell as it houses the genetic material (DNA).

 

• Ribosome (Option 3): Called the "protein factory" of the cell, as it is the site of protein synthesis.

 

• Plastid (Option 4): An organelle (e.g., chloroplast) involved in photosynthesis and storage in plant cells, not sorting/dispatch.

question: Which element of group 13 has the atomic number 113 and its electronic configuration is [Rn] 5f14 6d10 7s2 7p1?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nihonium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nihonium (Nh) has atomic number 113 and belongs to Group 13 (Boron family) of the periodic table, with the electronic configuration [Rn] 5f14 6d10 7s2 7p1. (निहोनियम — परमाणु क्रमांक 113)

 

• It is a synthetic (man-made) superheavy element, first synthesized in 2004 by a joint Russian-American team and independently confirmed by Japanese scientists at RIKEN in 2004.

 

• It was officially named Nihonium in 2016, after "Nihon", one of the Japanese names for Japan — making it the first element named after a country/place in Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Group 13 elements (Boron family) are: Boron (B), Aluminium (Al), Gallium (Ga), Indium (In), Thallium (Tl), and Nihonium (Nh).

 

• Nihonium is part of period 7 of the periodic table and is highly radioactive with an extremely short half-life.

 

NOTE

 

• Gallium (Option 1): Atomic number 31, a naturally occurring Group 13 element.

 

• Indium (Option 2): Atomic number 49, a naturally occurring Group 13 element used in touchscreens (ITO).

 

• Thallium (Option 4): Atomic number 81, a naturally occurring, toxic Group 13 element.

question: 54.6% of the total workforce is engaged in __________ and allied sector activites (Census of India 2011).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agriculture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, about 54.6% of India's total workforce was engaged in agriculture and allied activities (cultivators and agricultural labourers combined), making it the single largest employer in the country. (कृषि और संबद्ध क्षेत्र — जनगणना 2011)

 

• This is despite the fact that the agriculture sector's contribution to GDP is much lower (around 15-18%) than its share of employment, reflecting the phenomenon of disguised unemployment and low productivity in the sector.

 

• Of this, the Census classified workers as cultivators and agricultural labourers, together forming the majority of India's rural workforce.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The structural composition of India's economy shows a mismatch: agriculture employs the most people but contributes the least to GDP, while services contribute the most to GDP with relatively lower employment share.

 

• The next Census (originally due in 2021) has been delayed, so Census 2011 remains the latest official decadal data on workforce distribution.

 

NOTE

 

• Hunting and gathering (Option 1): Not a recognised Census occupational category for India's modern workforce.

 

• Manufacturing (Option 2): Falls under the secondary sector, employing a much smaller share of the workforce than agriculture.

 

• Mining (Option 4): A minor employer compared to agriculture, also part of the industrial/secondary sector.

question: Smriti Mandhana became the most expensive player in the Women's Indian Premier League with the ₹3.4 crore bid by ________ in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Royal Challengers Bangalore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the inaugural Women's Premier League (WPL) 2023 player auction, Smriti Mandhana was bought by Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB) for ₹3.4 crore, making her the most expensive player of the auction. (महिला प्रीमियर लीग — स्मृति मंधाना, RCB)

 

• The WPL 2023 was the first season of India's Women's Premier League cricket tournament, with five franchises: Mumbai Indians, Delhi Capitals, Gujarat Giants, UP Warriorz, and Royal Challengers Bangalore.

 

• Smriti Mandhana went on to captain Royal Challengers Bangalore in the tournament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mumbai Indians won the inaugural WPL 2023 title, defeating Delhi Capitals in the final.

 

• Other top buys at the WPL 2023 auction included Nat Sciver-Brunt (Mumbai Indians) and Ashleigh Gardner (Gujarat Giants).

 

NOTE

 

• Chennai Super Kings (Option 1): Did not field a team in WPL 2023 (CSK does not have a WPL franchise).

 

• Mumbai Indians (Option 3): Bought other top players like Nat Sciver-Brunt, not Mandhana.

 

• Rajasthan Royals (Option 4): Also does not have a WPL franchise.

question: Which state won the Indian Olympic Association's 'Best State' award at the 36th National Games in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maharashtra won the "Best State" award (Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy) from the Indian Olympic Association at the 36th National Games, held in Gujarat. (महाराष्ट्र — सर्वश्रेष्ठ राज्य ट्रॉफी, 36वें राष्ट्रीय खेल)

 

• This win ended a long gap, as Maharashtra reclaimed the top state honours after nearly three decades, topping the medal charts among the states (as opposed to institutional teams).

 

• The 36th National Games were held across multiple cities in Gujarat, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Services sports control board topped the overall medal tally at the 36th National Games for the fourth consecutive time, but the "Best State" trophy (among actual states) went to Maharashtra.

 

• The next edition, the 37th National Games, were held in Uttarakhand in 2025.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Did not win the Best State award at the 36th National Games.

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Did not win the Best State award at the 36th National Games.

 

• Haryana (Option 4): A strong sporting state, but did not win the Best State award at the 36th National Games.

question: Structural composition of the economy refers to:
option_1: contribution of various sectors to the GDP
option_4: rural and urban distribution of the population
solution_text:
The correct answer is contribution of various sectors to the GDP.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The structural composition of an economy refers to the relative share/contribution of the primary (agriculture), secondary (industry), and tertiary (services) sectors to the GDP of a country. (अर्थव्यवस्था की संरचनात्मक संरचना — GDP में क्षेत्रों का योगदान)

 

• It reflects how an economy is transforming — for example, a shift from an agriculture-dominated economy to an industry- or services-dominated one is called structural transformation.

 

• India's economy today shows a services-dominated structural composition in GDP terms, even though agriculture still employs the largest share of the workforce.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Colin Clark's three-sector theory classifies economic activities into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors to study structural change over time.

 

• A mismatch between a sector's share in GDP and its share in employment (as seen in Indian agriculture) is a key indicator studied in development economics.

 

NOTE

 

• Male-female distribution of the population (Option 2): Refers to the sex ratio, a demographic indicator, not economic structure.

 

• Private and public sectors classification (Option 3): Refers to ownership structure of enterprises, not sectoral GDP composition.

 

• Rural and urban distribution of the population (Option 4): Refers to urbanisation, a demographic/settlement indicator, not economic structure.

question: The rulers of which of the following Rajput dynasties patronised Jainism and one of them is reported to have accepted Jainism under the influence of a Jain scholar Hemachandra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chalukya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chalukya (Solanki) dynasty of Gujarat patronised Jainism, and its ruler Kumarapala is reported to have accepted Jainism under the influence of the renowned Jain scholar Hemachandra (Acharya Hemachandra). (चालुक्य वंश — कुमारपाल और हेमचंद्र)

 

• Hemachandra, also called "Kalikal Sarvajna", was a polymath scholar-monk of the Shvetambara Jain tradition at the Solanki court.

 

• Under Kumarapala's patronage, several Jain temples were built, and non-violence-related edicts (like bans on animal slaughter) were promoted in the kingdom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chalukyas (Solankis) of Gujarat, with their capital at Anhilwara (Patan), are also credited with building the Rani ki Vav (Queen's Stepwell), a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• Other Rajput dynasties of this period include the Pratiharas (Kannauj), Parmaras (Malwa), and Chahamanas/Chauhans (Ajmer-Delhi).

 

NOTE

 

• Pratihara (Option 1): A Rajput dynasty of Kannauj, primarily associated with the defence against Arab invasions, not Jainism/Hemachandra.

 

• Parmara (Option 2): Ruled Malwa (capital Dhara), known for patronising Sanskrit learning (e.g., Raja Bhoja), not this Jain conversion episode.

 

• Chahman (Option 4): The Chauhans of Ajmer-Delhi (e.g., Prithviraj Chauhan), not associated with Hemachandra's influence.

question: Padma Shri awardee of 2022, Nalini-Kamalini Asthana belongs to which of the following art genres?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nalini-Kamalini Asthana, twin sisters, are noted Kathak dance exponents from Lucknow, and they were jointly conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 for their contribution to the field of art. (नलिनी-कमलिनी अस्थाना — कथक नृत्य)

 

• They are known for their performances in the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak, having trained under illustrious gurus in the tradition.

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, conferred by the President of India for distinguished contributions in various fields.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Being twin recipients, Nalini and Kamalini Asthana are among the rare instances of siblings jointly honoured with the Padma Shri in the same year.

 

• The Padma Awards are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day and categorised into Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.

 

NOTE

 

• Painting (Option 1): Not the art form associated with the Asthana sisters.

 

• Sculpture (Option 2): Not the art form associated with the Asthana sisters.

 

• Architecture (Option 4): Not the art form associated with the Asthana sisters.

question: Since 2004, which of the following states in India is the permanent venue of International Film Festival of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Film Festival of India (IFFI) has had Goa as its permanent venue since 2004, and it is held every year in November. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय फिल्म महोत्सव — गोवा, स्थायी स्थल 2004 से)

 

• IFFI is organised jointly by the Directorate of Film Festivals (Ministry of Information and Broadcasting) and the Entertainment Society of Goa.

 

• Before Goa was made the permanent venue, IFFI used to be held in different cities across India on a rotational basis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• IFFI was first held in 1952 in Mumbai and is one of the oldest and most significant film festivals in Asia.

 

• Goa also hosts other major cultural events, and IFFI screens films across categories such as the International Competition Section, Indian Panorama, and retrospectives.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Not the venue of IFFI.

 

• New Delhi (Option 2): Was one of the earlier rotational venues before 2004, but is not the current permanent venue.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Mumbai hosted the first IFFI in 1952, but is not the permanent venue since 2004.

question: Who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for founding the Grameen Bank and pioneering the concepts of microcredit and microfinance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Yunus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Muhammad Yunus, a Bangladeshi economist, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006 jointly with the Grameen Bank he founded, for pioneering the concepts of microcredit and microfinance. (मोहम्मद यूनुस — ग्रामीण बैंक, नोबेल शांति पुरस्कार 2006)

 

• He founded the Grameen Bank in Bangladesh in 1983, providing small loans (microcredit) to poor individuals, especially women, without requiring collateral, to help them start income-generating activities.

 

• He is often called the "Banker to the Poor", also the title of his well-known autobiography.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded by the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo, unlike other Nobel Prizes awarded in Stockholm, Sweden.

 

• Muhammad Yunus later served as the Chief Adviser of the interim government of Bangladesh starting in 2024.

 

NOTE

 

• Muhammad Yusuf (Option 1):, Muhammad Wasim (Option 3), and Muhammad Asif (Option 4): These are distractor names and are not associated with the Grameen Bank or the Nobel Peace Prize.

question: Exports of mangoes by India is a part of ________ method of measurement of its national income.
solution_text:
The correct answer is expenditure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The expenditure method of measuring national income sums up total spending in the economy as GDP = C + I + G + (X - M), where X (exports) is one of its components. (व्यय विधि — निर्यात, राष्ट्रीय आय का मापन)

 

• Since exports of mangoes represent spending by foreign buyers on India's output, they form part of the (X - M) — net exports — component of the expenditure method.

 

• The three standard methods to measure national income are the Product/Value Added method, the Income method, and the Expenditure method; each should ideally give the same final GDP figure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Income method sums factor incomes (wages, rent, interest, profit) earned by all factors of production.

 

• The Value Added (Product) method sums the value added at each stage of production across all sectors of the economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Circular income (Option 1): Not a standard method of national income measurement; refers loosely to the circular flow of income concept.

 

• Value added (Option 2): This is the production method, which measures value added at each stage of production, not exports specifically.

 

• Income (Option 4): The income method captures factor incomes earned domestically, not export earnings directly.

question: According to Census of India 2011, which state in India has the highest proportion of its population living in the urban areas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Goa had the highest urbanisation rate among Indian states, with about 62.17% of its population living in urban areas. (गोवा — सर्वाधिक शहरीकरण दर, जनगणना 2011)

 

• Among Union Territories, Delhi had the highest urban population proportion (nearly 97.5%), but the question specifically asks about states.

 

• India's overall urban population share as per Census 2011 was about 31.16% of the total population.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• After Goa, Mizoram and Tamil Nadu were among the next most urbanised states as per Census 2011.

 

• The least urbanised major state as per Census 2011 was Himachal Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Highly developed but not the most urbanised state by Census definition (~47.7%).

 

• Haryana (Option 2): Urbanisation around 34.9%, lower than Goa.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Highly urbanised (~48.4%) but still lower than Goa's rate.

question: Which is the biggest tributary of the upper Brahmaputra that originates in the Tibetan Himalayas and winds its way into India through Arunachal Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subansiri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Subansiri River is the biggest tributary of the upper Brahmaputra, originating in the Tibetan Himalayas and entering India through Arunachal Pradesh. (सुबनसिरी नदी — ब्रह्मपुत्र की सबसे बड़ी सहायक नदी)

 

• The name "Subansiri" means "river of gold", referring to the gold dust once found in its waters.

 

• It joins the Brahmaputra in Assam, and the Subansiri Lower Hydroelectric Project (India's largest hydropower project) is being built on this river.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major tributaries of the Brahmaputra include the Dibang, Lohit, Kameng, Manas, and Teesta.

 

• The Brahmaputra itself originates near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet, where it is known as the Tsangpo/Yarlung Tsangpo, before entering India through Arunachal Pradesh (where it is called the Siang/Dihang).

 

NOTE

 

• Yerla (Option 2): A tributary of the Krishna River in Maharashtra, unrelated to the Brahmaputra.

 

• Musi (Option 3): A tributary of the Krishna River, flowing through Hyderabad, Telangana.

 

• Aner (Option 4): A tributary of the Tapi River in Maharashtra, unrelated to the Brahmaputra.

question: Which colour of light from VIBGYOR has minimum energy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Red.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Among the seven colours of VIBGYOR (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red), Red has the longest wavelength and hence the lowest frequency, giving it the minimum energy according to Planck's relation E = hf. (लाल रंग — न्यूनतम ऊर्जा, अधिकतम तरंगदैर्घ्य)

 

• Energy of light is directly proportional to frequency and inversely proportional to wavelength; since red light has the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum (~700 nm), it carries the least energy per photon.

 

• Violet, with the shortest wavelength (~400 nm) and highest frequency, carries the maximum energy among visible colours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• VIBGYOR is the mnemonic for the sequence of colours seen in a rainbow/visible spectrum: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red.

 

• This dispersion of white light into VIBGYOR colours through a prism was first demonstrated by Sir Isaac Newton.

 

NOTE

 

• Green (Option 1): Has intermediate wavelength/energy, not the minimum.

 

• Violet (Option 2): Has the maximum energy (shortest wavelength) among VIBGYOR, the opposite of what's asked.

 

• Yellow (Option 3): Has intermediate wavelength/energy, not the minimum.

question: Tulip Festival is famous in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Srinagar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tulip Festival is famously celebrated in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, at the Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden, held annually in spring (March-April). (श्रीनगर — इंदिरा गांधी मेमोरियल ट्यूलिप गार्डन)

 

• The Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden, located on the foothills of the Zabarwan Range overlooking the Dal Lake, is Asia's largest tulip garden.

 

• The festival showcases lakhs of tulip bulbs of numerous varieties and colours and is a major tourism attraction promoting spring tourism in Kashmir.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The garden was formerly known as the Model Floriculture Centre before being renamed after former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

 

• Kashmir's Tulip Festival is often used to promote the region's tourism sector and coincides with the broader spring blooming season, alongside almond blossoms.

 

NOTE

 

• Agra (Option 1): Famous for the Taj Mahal, not the Tulip Festival.

 

• Allahabad/Prayagraj (Option 2): Famous for the Kumbh Mela, not the Tulip Festival.

 

• Ludhiana (Option 3): An industrial city in Punjab, not associated with the Tulip Festival.

question: In August 2021, Ram Nath Kovind granted assent to which Constitution Amendment Act empowering states and UTs to identify and specify Socially and Educationally Backward Classes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 105th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (One Hundred and Fifth Amendment) Act, 2021, assented to by President Ram Nath Kovind in August 2021, restored the power of States and Union Territories to identify and specify Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs) in their own lists. (105वां संविधान संशोधन — राज्यों को SEBC सूची का अधिकार)

 

• This amendment reversed the effect of the Supreme Court's Maratha reservation judgment (2021), which had held that only the central government (through the National Commission for Backward Classes) could identify SEBCs after the 102nd Amendment.

 

• It amended Articles 342A and 366(26c) to clarify that states retain the power to maintain their own separate SEBC lists for state-level reservations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 had given constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).

 

• The 105th Amendment was passed to address the concerns raised by several states after the Supreme Court's interpretation restricted their power to create backward class lists.

 

NOTE

 

• 104th (Option 2): Related to the extension/discontinuation of reservation for Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies (2020), not SEBC identification.

 

• 103rd (Option 3): Introduced 10% EWS reservation for economically weaker sections (2019), not SEBC identification.

 

• 102nd (Option 4): Gave constitutional status to the NCBC; its interpretation is what the 105th Amendment later corrected.

question: In which of the following economic accounts are transfer payments included?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government account.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Transfer payments (such as pensions, subsidies, and unemployment benefits) are unrequited payments made without any corresponding good/service in return, and in the system of social accounting they are recorded in the Government account, as the government is the principal source of such payments. (हस्तांतरण भुगतान — सरकारी खाता)

 

• Since transfer payments do not correspond to any current production of goods or services, they are excluded from GDP calculated via the expenditure/income method, but are still tracked as an expenditure item within the government's accounts.

 

• The Government account in social accounting records the government's receipts (taxes) and expenditures (including transfer payments, subsidies, and purchases of goods/services).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of transfer payments include old-age pensions, scholarships, unemployment allowances, and interest on public debt (in some classifications).

 

• Social accounting divides the economy into sectors such as Household, Firm/Production, Government, and Rest of the World accounts, each recording specific types of income and expenditure flows.

 

NOTE

 

• Household account (Option 2): Records household income (wages, rent, interest, profit) and consumption expenditure, not the source of transfer payments.

 

• Appropriation account (Option 3): Records how a firm's/corporation's profits are distributed (dividends, retained earnings, taxes), unrelated to transfer payments.

 

• Production account (Option 4): Records the value of output produced and inputs used by firms, not transfer payments.

question: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, now known as Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, was first enacted in the year______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2005.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) was enacted by the Parliament of India in 2005 and notified/implemented in phases starting February 2006. (राष्ट्रीय ग्रामीण रोजगार गारंटी अधिनियम — 2005)

 

• It guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

 

• The Act was renamed the "Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)" in 2009, on the occasion of the 20th anniversary of the scheme's inception plans, though the founding legislation dates to 2005.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• MGNREGA is implemented under the Ministry of Rural Development and is often cited as the world's largest work guarantee programme.

 

• The scheme mandates that at least one-third of the beneficiaries be women.

 

NOTE

 

• 2000 (Option 1): Predates the enactment of NREGA.

 

• 2009 (Option 3): The year the Act was renamed MGNREGA, not the year of its original enactment.

 

• 2014 (Option 4): Not associated with the enactment or renaming of the Act.

question:
The celebration of Christmas, Eid and Holi in school is an example of making children learn fundamental duties as well.

Which of the following fundamental duties advocates about this type of ideals?
option_1: To defend the country and render national service
option_3: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
option_4: To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood
solution_text:
The correct answer is To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A(e) of the Indian Constitution lays down the fundamental duty "to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities". (सामान्य भाईचारे की भावना — अनुच्छेद 51A(e))

 

• Celebrating festivals of different religions like Christmas, Eid, and Holi together in schools instils in children a sense of communal harmony and unity in diversity, directly reflecting this fundamental duty.

 

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution via the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee, under Part IVA (Article 51A).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed in Article 51A; the 11th (relating to providing education to children aged 6-14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be directly enforced by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

NOTE

 

• To defend the country and render national service (Option 1): Article 51A(d), relates to national defence duties, not religious/cultural harmony.

 

• To develop the scientific temper (Option 2): Article 51A(h), relates to promoting scientific temper and humanism, not festival celebration for harmony.

 

• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence (Option 3): Article 51A(i), relates to protecting public property and non-violence, not communal harmony through festivals.

question: Which of the following states is NOT a part of the Peninsular Plateau in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Peninsular Plateau is one of India's oldest and most stable landmasses, covering much of peninsular India, but Punjab lies in the Indo-Gangetic (Northern) Plains, not on the plateau. (प्रायद्वीपीय पठार — पंजाब इसमें शामिल नहीं)

 

• Punjab is part of the fertile alluvial plains formed by the Indus river system tributaries (Sutlej, Beas, Ravi), a very different geological formation from the ancient Gondwana-era Peninsular Plateau.

 

• States that are part of the Peninsular Plateau include Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, and Odisha (in parts).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Peninsular Plateau is divided into the Central Highlands (north of the Narmada) and the Deccan Plateau (south of the Narmada), and is composed of ancient igneous and metamorphic rocks.

 

• The Peninsular Plateau is bordered by the Aravalli Range in the northwest, the Western Ghats in the west, and the Eastern Ghats in the east.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Located on the Deccan Plateau, part of the Peninsular Plateau.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Located on the Central Highlands, part of the Peninsular Plateau.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Located on the southern Deccan Plateau, part of the Peninsular Plateau.

question:
Poshan Abhiyaan is a programme to achieve nutritional status of children from 0 to 6 years.

Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for raising the nutrition level?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 47.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 47 of the Indian Constitution, a Directive Principle of State Policy, states that it is the duty of the State to "raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and to improve public health". (अनुच्छेद 47 — पोषण स्तर बढ़ाना)

 

• Poshan Abhiyaan (National Nutrition Mission), launched in 2018, aims to improve the nutritional status of children (0-6 years), adolescent girls, pregnant women and lactating mothers, directly aligning with the goal set out in Article 47.

 

• Article 47 also directs the State to work towards prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) are contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution and are non-justiciable but fundamental in governance.

 

• Poshan Abhiyaan is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development and uses technology, targeted convergence, and community mobilisation to reduce malnutrition, anaemia, and stunting.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 44 (Option 2): Relates to the State's endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code, unrelated to nutrition.

 

• Article 46 (Option 3): Relates to promotion of educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and other weaker sections, unrelated to nutrition.

 

• Article 45 (Option 4): Relates to provision for early childhood care and education for children below 6 years, distinct from nutrition levels specifically.

question: Who among the following is the first Indian female football player to play in Union of European Football Association (UEFA)'s women's champions league?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manisha Kalyan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Manisha Kalyan became the first Indian female footballer to play in the UEFA Women's Champions League, representing Apollon Ladies FC of Cyprus in a qualifying round match in August 2022. (मनीषा कल्याण — पहली भारतीय महिला फुटबॉलर, UEFA चैंपियंस लीग)

 

• She hails from Punjab and had been a key member of the Indian women's national football team before moving abroad to play in Europe.

 

• Her achievement marked a milestone for Indian women's football, being the first instance of an Indian woman footballer competing in Europe's premier women's club competition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manisha Kalyan later also became the first Indian footballer (male or female) to play in a major European league, joining clubs in Cyprus's top division.

 

• The UEFA Women's Champions League is the top-tier European club competition for women's football, first held in the 2001-02 season.

 

NOTE

 

• Shanti Mallick (Option 1): Not associated with UEFA Women's Champions League participation.

 

• Bala Devi (Option 2): The first Indian footballer (male or female) to sign for a top-tier European club (Rangers FC, Scotland, in 2020), but not the first to play in the UEFA Women's Champions League.

 

• Oinam Bembem Devi (Option 4): A celebrated former captain of the Indian women's football team, but not associated with the UEFA Women's Champions League.

question: Ustad Asad Ali Khan played which of the following instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rudra Veena.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Asad Ali Khan (1937-2011) was one of India's foremost Rudra Veena players, belonging to the Rudra Veena gharana of the Khandarbani tradition. (रुद्र वीणा — उस्ताद असद अली खान)

 

• He was a recipient of the Padma Bhushan (2008) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, celebrated for keeping the ancient and endangered art of Rudra Veena playing alive.

 

• The Rudra Veena is one of the oldest string instruments of India, traditionally associated with the Dhrupad style of Hindustani classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ustad Asad Ali Khan devoted his life to teaching students the Rudra Veena, an instrument that had become rare by the 20th century.

 

• The Rudra Veena consists of two large resonating gourds and a long hollow stem, and is played while seated on the floor.

 

NOTE

 

• Algoza (Option 2): A pair of wind instruments popular in Punjab and Rajasthan folk music, not played by Asad Ali Khan.

 

• Sitar (Option 3): A plucked string instrument popularised by artists like Ravi Shankar and Vilayat Khan, not the instrument Asad Ali Khan was known for.

 

• Ravanahatha (Option 4): An ancient bowed folk string instrument from Rajasthan, not played by Asad Ali Khan.
